messages:
sec-alert-bot: ALERT: public object discovered: gs://redwood-backups/redis-nightly/redis-2026-03-20.rdb (scanner: public-bucket-crawler)
sec-alert-bot: rule=public-bucket-obj severity=high detected_by=external_crawler
maria: copying alert here. anyone on call? this looks like an RDB in a backups bucket, possibly creds inside.
tyler: I'm on it. which project/sa created the export job? tagging @kevin
kevin: I deployed the nightly-export job. It uses sa:infra-backups@redwood-infer. The job writes to gs://redwood-backups. I thought bucket was private. running quick checks now.
kevin: `gsutil acl get gs://redwood-backups | head` shows userACLs present. hmm terraform expected uniformBucketLevelAccess=true
tyler: looks like terraform drift — uniform bucket-level access got disabled during a manual change months ago. possible cause: a one-off migration.
maria: potential data exposure = high. action plan: 1) contain (make object/bucket private), 2) audit who accessed, 3) rotate any keys/tokens referenced in the snapshot if present, 4) notify security/PMs/legal if PII.
kevin: containment steps I'm running:
kevin: `gsutil iam ch -d allUsers:objectViewer gs://redwood-backups` -> removes public binding
kevin: `gsutil acl set private gs://redwood-backups/redis-nightly/redis-2026-03-20.rdb` -> setting object private
kevin: added a temp bucket policy to deny public access and enabled uniform bucket-level access via Terraform driftfix branch.
tyler: good. also toggled retention so object can't be deleted accidentally while we investigate: `gsutil retention set 7d gs://redwood-backups` (holding for 7 days)
maria: who might have downloaded it? can we get access logs? enable object access logs and run a report.
kevin: GCS access logs were not enabled for that bucket (😭). However Cloud Audit Logs for storage.googleapis.com show `storage.objects.get` events. pulling logs now.
kevin: found two external IPs that hit the object at 03:12 UTC yesterday — one from a corporate IP, one from outside our CIDR range. exporting logs: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=gs_bucket AND protoPayload.methodName=storage.objects.get AND resource.labels.bucket_name=redwood-backups" --limit 200`.
kevin: external IP resolved to a hosting provider; looks like the public scan crawler. no signin tokens in logs so far.
maria: ok. next: inspect the RDB for secrets. do we have a safe sandbox to open the snapshot? we should not open on developer machines.
tyler: I'll spin up an isolated GCP project with no network egress and mount the RDB, run `redis-check-rdb --command` to inspect strings. job: infra/backup-forensics-1998
kevin: pulled a copy into the isolated project. grep for "AKIA|AIza|ssh-rsa|PRIVATE KEY" inside dumped strings.
kevin: results: found a single line that looks like a service account key JSON embedded in application logs inside the RDB values. not a user password but a service account key id.
maria: treat as potentially compromised. action: rotate that service account keys immediately and revoke the old key. Which SA?
kevin: infra-backups@redwood-infer. suspected key id: 0123456789abcdef. I'm revoking now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=infra-backups@redwood-infer.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
tyler: also update any jobs that used that key to use Workload Identity / short-lived tokens instead. ticketing infra-987 for keyless transition.
jess: legal here — do we have any regulatory data in the snapshot? if yes, we'll need to prepare customer notification templates. @olivia please advise product/PMs.
olivia: Product: checking dataset tagging for redis namespace. prelim indicates no PII buckets keyed, but we'll do a thorough scan. stand by.
maria: communications: we should prepare an internal postmortem and an external customer note only if PII present. timeline and containment steps recorded. also record the Terraform drift and fix.
kevin: added terraform change to repo: `set uniform_bucket_level_access = true` and added lifecycle rule to prevent manual ACL changes. PR -> infra/driftfix #412
tyler: follow-ups:
- enable GCS access logs and bucket-level audit exports to BigQuery (owner: kevin)
- run repo-wide scan for any other backup buckets without uniform access (owner: tyler)
- rotate any SA keys found in snapshots (owner: maria)
- update runbooks and add a detection for exported RDB objects in public buckets (owner: sec-eng)
maria: legal notified, infra actions assigned. immediate containment done. we should meet for a 30-min incident sync in 15m to coordinate comms.
jess: acknowleged. add me to the sync.
olivia: adding PM/ops to the sync too.
sec-alert-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATED id=inc-1998012345 status=contained
maria: reopening once we've confirmed no downstream downloads from external IPs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
